title: [diffusion] optimization: transfer mapped layers through a courier thread
body:
A copy whose source is a checkpoint mapping is synchronous however it is requested — the driver stages unpinned memory through its own buffer — and the prefetch hooks run on the compute thread, so every mapped layer stalled the denoise step for its whole transfer. This adds a courier: a worker thread that stages a mapped layer's bytes into one of two pinned slots (a plain memcpy when the page cache holds them) and issues the device copy on its own stream, where it is genuinely asynchronous. Parameters are still rebound on the compute thread at collect time, so module state is never touched concurrently; blocking callers and any courier failure keep the direct synchronous path.

body:
## Purpose

The NIXL EPLB communicator previously allocated `local_moe_layer_size * ep_size` for its send buffer to handle the worst case where a rank sends all its experts to every peer. For DeepSeek-V3.2 with EP=8 this added ~14 GiB of overhead.

title: [diffusion] feat: capture-safe pynccl all-to-all
body:
## Motivation

A CUDA graph cannot hold a `torch.distributed` ProcessGroupNCCL collective: its host-side per-op bookkeeping advances once at capture and never again, so on replay the ranks stop agreeing about which collective is in flight and hang. This is the reason whole-forward DiT capture (#31852) must refuse sharded runs today, and it is not a NCCL limitation — srt already runs collectives inside captured regions by calling raw nccl through its `pynccl` wrapper, which carries no per-call host state. The diffusion tree's vendored `pynccl` lacked both an all-to-all and the capture-window switch.

title: [Kernel][Model][MiniMax-M3] Add per-rank context-parallel sparse indexer scoring Triton kernel
body:
## Purpose

Add a Triton module that computes MiniMax-M3 sparse indexer context scores independently per context-parallel (CP) rank, opt-in and decoupled from the global DCP configuration.

The new `indexer_context_scores` helper (backed by the `_context_score` Triton kernel) assigns logical KV blocks round-robin across ranks (`block = local * world + rank`) so each rank only scores the shard of context it owns. It returns a `[heads, tokens, ceil(blocks/world)]` float32 score tensor. Inputs are strictly validated:

- Queries must be BF16 `[tokens, heads, 128]` with a contiguous D dimension.
- Index cache must be contiguous `[pages, 128, 128]` in BF16, FP8 `e4m3fn`, or FP8 `e4m3fnuz`.
- Block table and sequence lengths must be int32; the block table must cover the requested context.
- All inputs must live on the same GPU.

title: Fix NaN in triton EAGLE spec-v2 draft-extend CUDA graph at topk>1 (wrong qo_indptr stride)
body:
The draft-extend CUDA-graph metadata built `qo_indptr` with a per-req stride of `num_steps+1`, but the runner lays out `num_draft_tokens` tokens/req. For topk>1 these differ, so at bs>1 each req's queries read from the wrong offset -> NaN (bs==1 and eager are unaffected). Use `num_draft_tokens` for the v2 draft-extend path.
